newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end quiet day with large gains.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end quiet day with large gains.

text.p: U.S. debt futures finished a quiet session with sizable gains, boosted by U.S. economic data that was weaker than anticipated.
U.S. durable goods orders in November fell 1.6 percent compared to expectations for a 0.1 percent increase.
"Durable goods were weaker than expected, but we've been in a tight range all week," said one analyst at a large U.S. brokerage house.
The weak data extended that range slightly, sending the March bond above minor chart resistance near 113-20/32.
But little followthrough developed and prices subsequently languished in a narrow range.
Traders said there was insufficient momentum on the rally to push the nearby Treasury bond contract above further chart resistance at about 114-01/32 to 114-06/32.
Volume was heavier than the prior two sessions surrounding the Christmas holiday, but still very light as many traders extended seasonal holidays, traders said.
Jobless claims data was also released this morning, falling to 335,000 compared to expectations for a decline to 346,000 from a revised 350,000 in the prior week.

Trade could remain light next week ahead of the New Year's holiday, but "it will be interesting to see what happens next week when some more people come back to work," said Jim Collins, senior vice president at Smith Barney Harris Upham and Co.
The Chicago Purchasing Managers' December index will be released Tuesday and will give the market its first glimpse of data from December.
Debt futures market close early Tuesday and are closed all day Wednesday for the New Year's holiday.

At settlement, March T-bond futures were up 19/32 at 113-30/32, 10-year T-notes were 10/32 higher at 109-30/32 and muni-bonds were 26/32 higher at 117-00/32. March IMM T-bills were two basis points higher at 94.98 and Eurodollars were up two points at 94.47. ((--Chicago Derivatives desk (312)408-8750)) ((E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com))
